# hackage2buck

this is a tool kind of like hackage2nix, but for a desired subset of hackage.
cabal is used to produce a valid build plan, which this tool then consumes to generate a BUCK file to build all relevant hackage packages.

it materializes a cabal project in `third_party/haskell/stub` including `stub.cabal`.
version bounds are injected via `cabal.project` and frozen by cabal into a final resolved set in `cabal.project.freeze`.

then, hackage2buck comes in.

## input

## output

```python
# @generated by //third_party/haskell/hackage2buck
load("//third_party/haskell:defs.bzl", "boot_package", "third_party_haskell_library")

# one per boot package. provides a flat namespace for all haskell packages
# including boot ones
boot_package(name = "base")  # alias -> toolchains//haskell:base + haskell_package_info target
boot_package(name = "transformers")

third_party_haskell_library(
    name = "distributive",
    version = "0.6.2.1",
    sha256 = "d7351392e0...",
    hs_source_dirs = ["src"],
    srcs = [
        "src/Data/Distributive.hs",
        "src/Data/Distributive/Generic.hs",
    ],
    deps = [":base", ":base-orphans", ":tagged", ":transformers"],
    compiler_flags = ["-XHaskell2010"],
    public = True,   # visibility PUBLIC; non-public targets stay package-local
)
```

what third_party_haskell_library expands to:

```python
http_archive(
    name = "{name}.tar.gz",
    strip_prefix = "{name}-{ver}",
    url = "https://hackage.haskell.org/package/{pkg}-{ver}/{pkg}-{ver}.tar.gz",
    sub_targets = srcs + c_srcs + hsc_srcs + include_dirs,
)

# emits a c header with the MIN_VERSION_foo defines in it + tset for further
# ones to produce their own headers
haskell_package_info(
    name = "{name}.info",
    package_name = "{name}",
    version = "{ver}",
    deps = [d + ".info" for d in deps],
)

haskell_library(
    name = "{name}",
    deps = ["{name}.info", ...],
    srcs = ["{name}.tar.gz[src/Foo/Bar.hs]", ...],
    ...
```
